answer: In a decentralized network of autonomous entities akin to a digital meadow, Proof-of-Stake protocols provide robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity creation to financial capital rather than computational ease. An attacker attempting to flood the system with fraudulent agents finds the approach hollow because validator weight scales strictly with locked economic stake. Deploying thousands of fake nodes remains nothing more than a computational fable; the economic cost to the adversary scales linearly with the total value locked, making majority capture prohibitively expensive.
